West Texas Intermediate crude jumped 3.7% to $105.12 a barrel after Saudi Aramco canceled or delayed cargoes to European refiners.
Brent crude rose 2.4% to $108.20. Heating oil surged 5.5% and gasoline futures climbed 3.2%, with U.S. diesel prices now averaging $6.26 a gallon, surpassing the previous record set in 2022.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose for the fifth straight session, climbing to 5.04% before settling near 5.00%. The 30-year yield stood at 5.37% and the 20-year at 5.40%.

Traders are assigning roughly a 92% probability to a 25-basis-point rate hike from the Federal Reserve on Wednesday, which would be the first increase since July 2023.
Across U.S. equity markets by midday Tuesday, losses were broad-based but orderly, with nine of 11 S&P 500 sectors lower.
The S&P 500 slipped 0.5% to 7,580.85, hitting its lowest level in three weeks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was the clear laggard, shedding 496 points, or 1%, to 51,925.70.
The Nasdaq 100 fell 0.6% to 28,946.97. Gold eased 0.2% to $4,290.64 an ounce, leaving the metal down 2.8% over the past month as a fifth straight day of dollar gains capped bullion.
